subject.title: Altadena Library District Board, Trustee Area 3

text: As a lifelong learner, I have relied on libraries throughout my academic and professional journey. For the past 15 years, I have worked as a registered nurse, a profession that values continuous learning and service.
I began my nursing education at L.A. General Medical Center, where I discovered my passion for serving the underrepresented communities.

After graduation, I joined the Emergency Department and later earned a Bachelor of Science in Nursing, a Master of Science as an Acute Care Nurse Practitioner, and a post-master's certificate as a Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner. Today, I serve as the Program Coordinator and Lead Educator for the Emergency Nurse Training Program.

My experience caring for marginalized populations has reinforced the essential role public libraries play in strengthening communities. This is especially true as Altadena recovers from the Eaton Fire. Libraries provide access to information, technology, educational opportunities, and welcoming spaces that foster connection, resilience, and lifelong learning.

I would be honored to serve as a Trustee for the Altadena Library Board. I am committed to supporting equitable access to library resources and ensuring our libraries continue to meet the evolving needs of our diverse community as we rebuild and move forward together.

text: Occupation: Clinical Assoc. Professor of S.W.

Hi. I raised my daughter for 19 years in Altadena – she went to Aveson, Pasadena High, and CSArts – and we have been grateful library users. We live within walking distance of the main library, and visited several times a week for years. Now that she is at Cal State, I am excited to ask for your vote as Trustee so I can be as helpful to our libraries as they are for us.

I work as an associate professor of social work, and believe in the community-first purposes of our libraries. Whether for doing research, reading, listening to music, watching DVDs, children's groups, using the on-line computers, visiting for cultural events, getting our passports, notarizing post-fire SCE documents, even as a place for air conditioning, our libraries are an incredibly helpful public resource in our lives. As an academic, I am committed to keeping our libraries open, expansive, diverse and useful!

Our main library is, unfortunately, closed for needed renovations. These will improve the branch, but the process needs strong oversight. I am a former senior project manager for LAUSD's facilities division, and my experience is another reason I can be a helpful Trustee.

text: I have lived in Altadena for 39 years. I'm seeking a position on the Altadena Library District Board of Trustees because I am an ardent advocate of the importance of libraries to democratic societies and a believer in libraries' ability to provide access to information and ongoing learning freely to all who visit.

After the January 2025 Eaton Fire, when my wife and I were able to return after evacuation, naturally our first priority was to check on our residence. It was standing. Our next stop was to check on the Main Altadena Library branch, located a few blocks from our home. We were relieved to find it also was still standing.

Since retiring 10 years ago, I have served on several non-profit boards, Including the Los Angeles Conservancy, Las Angelitas del Pueblo, and the Altadena Historical Society. I believe this experience has prepared me well to serve as a trustee on the Altadena Library Board.
As Altadena rebuilds and reimagines its future, I am eager to support the Library Board, in an official capacity, as that work progresses.
